Subject: Quick ask — 10 day runway vs surge credits for pilot

Hi Karthik,

Quick note from the ops side at Navisys — we had an unplanned spike in inference during the last QA run and we are going to exhaust the pilot capacity a few days earlier than expected. We have two asks and would like to know which is cleaner from a procurement/contracting point of view:

- Option A: Add 10 calendar days to the existing time-boxed pilot (no change to SKUs, same daily access window).
- Option B: Keep pilot end date fixed, purchase a short "surge pack" (one-week burst of added tokens/hours) and invoice as a separate one-time item.

From our side, procurement prefers a one-time invoice (Option B) because it doesn't require amending the pilot dates. Legal said they can do either but want clear pricing and a simple SOW amendment if we change dates.

Can you propose pricing and any operational differences (e.g., how caching/kv-cache warm up behaves if we do a one-week burst vs extending the pilot window)? We need a path that keeps the pilot results comparable for our product team.

Thanks — appreciate a quick turnaround, we are aiming to be live with the evaluation signals by Aug 20.

Elena

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear summary. Short answer up front: Option B (surge pack) is usually cleaner operationally and legally; Option A is simpler for metrics continuity but requires an amendment. Details below and a draft quote attached.

Operational differences:
- Surge pack (Option B): We provision a temporary capacity tranche routed to your pilot project. KV-cache and prefix cache are preserved for the pilot model so inference latency/profile should remain consistent; however, bursts allocate additional workers which can change observed p99 latency slightly (usually improves with more parallel workers). No SSO or auth changes required; invoice as a one-time line item.
- Time extension (Option A): Keeps a single uninterrupted pilot timeframe which makes downstream A/B comparisons simpler (same model version and deployment). This requires a short addendum to the pilot SOW (we can generate a 1-paragraph amendment).

Pricing (draft):
- Option B: 7-day surge pack = $8,500 (one-time), includes up to 75% additional concurrent throughput cap and 40M extra tokens; 10% discount for pilots converting to Dedicated within 90 days.
- Option A: 10-day extension = pro-rated pilot daily rate = $9,400 (pro-rata), no additional discounting.

Recommendation: If procurement wants to avoid contract amendments, go with Option B (surge pack) — we'll keep telemetry consistent and provide a short note about performance variance. If the pilot results must be on a continuous date range for the product experiment, take Option A.

Attached: 2026-08-05-navisys-bridge-quote.pdf (line items + quick T&Cs) and a one-page runbook note.

I'll loop in Jordan for any pricing flexibility and Marissa if we need to coordinate finance. Happy to hop on a 20m sync if you want to review live.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
